units.text: INT. GHOSTS - CONTINUOUS
No, I should think not.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: But what is the general feeling in the neighbourhood? You, of course, know better than I.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Well--the general feeling--
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Is there any considerable number of people--really responsible people--who might be scandalised?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: What do you mean by "really responsible people"?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Well, I mean people in such independent and influential positions that one cannot help attaching some weight to their opinions.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: There are several people of that sort here, who would very likely be shocked if--
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: There, you see! In town we have many such people. Think of all my colleague's adherents! People would be only too ready to interpret our action as a sign that neither you nor I had the right faith in a Higher Providence.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: But for your own part, my dear Pastor, you can at least tell yourself that--
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Yes, I know--I know; my conscience would be quite easy, that is true enough. But nevertheless we should not escape grave misinterpretation; and that might very likely react unfavourably upon the Orphanage.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Well, in that case--
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Nor can I entirely lose sight of the difficult--I may even say painful--position in which I might perhaps be placed. In the leading circles of the town, people take a lively interest in this Orphanage. It is, of course, founded partly for the benefit of the town, as well; and it is to be hoped it will, to a considerable extent, result in lightening our Poor Rates. Now, as I have been your adviser, and have had the business arrangements in my hands, I cannot but fear that I may have to bear the brunt of fanaticism--
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Oh, you mustn't run the risk of that.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: To say nothing of the attacks that would assuredly be made upon me in certain papers and periodicals, which--
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Enough, my dear Pastor Manders. That consideration is quite decisive.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Then you do not wish the Orphanage to be insured?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: No. We will let it alone.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Leaning back in his chair.
But if, now, a disaster were to happen? One can never tell--Should you be able to make good the damage?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: No; I tell you plainly I should do nothing of the kind.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Then I must tell you, Mrs. Alving--we are taking no small responsibility upon ourselves.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Do you think we can do otherwise?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: No, that is just the point; we really cannot do otherwise. We ought not to expose ourselves to misinterpretation; and we have no right whatever to give offence to the weaker brethren.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: You, as a clergyman, certainly should not.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: I really think, too, we may trust that such an institution has fortune on its side; in fact, that it stands under a special providence.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Let us hope so, Pastor Manders.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Then we will let it take its chance?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Yes, certainly.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Very well. So be it.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Makes a note.
Then--no insurance.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: It's odd that you should just happen to mention the matter to-day--
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: I have often thought of asking you about it--
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: --for we very nearly had a fire down there yesterday.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: You don't say so!
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Oh, it was a trifling matter. A heap of shavings had caught fire in the carpenter's workshop.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Where Engstrand works?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Yes. They say he's often very careless with matches.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: He has so much on his mind, that man--so many things to fight against. Thank God, he is now striving to lead a decent life, I hear.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Indeed! Who says so?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: He himself assures me of it. And he is certainly a capital workman.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Oh, yes; so long as he's sober--
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Ah, that melancholy weakness! But, he is often driven to it by his injured leg, he says. Last time he was in town I was really touched by him. He came and thanked me so warmly for having got him work here, so that he might be near Regina.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: He doesn't see much of her.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Oh, yes; he has a talk with her every day. He told me so himself.
units.name: MANDERS
